title: Tic-Tac-Toe Board Wiring Bug
description:
## Problem Statement

You're an engineer on the CoderX Games team. Yesterday your teammate shipped the new Tic-Tac-Toe widget, and QA filed a bug ticket right away: *"Clicks don't behave — the first square seems to do nothing, and later moves look like they land in the wrong square. Games never reach a winner or a draw."*

Your job: dig through the codebase, find the wiring bug, and fix it so the game plays correctly.

The widget is split across a few modules, the same way the real feature repo is laid out:

- `src/components/Square.jsx` — renders a single playable cell (`button.square`).
- `src/components/Board.jsx` — renders the 3x3 grid of `Square` cells and reports clicks.
- `src/utils/winner.js` — `computeWinner(squares)` returns `'X'`, `'O'`, or `null`.
- `src/App.jsx` — owns the game state: the board array, whose turn it is, who won, and draw detection.

When the bug is fixed, the widget must behave like this:

1. A 3x3 board of empty cells renders on load.
2. Clicking an empty cell writes the current player's mark (`X` starts).
3. Players alternate — every click flips the turn from `X` to `O` and back.
4. A cell that already has a mark can never be overwritten (and the turn doesn't change).
5. A winning line — any row, column, or diagonal — ends the game, the status reads `Winner: X` / `Winner: O`, and further clicks are ignored.
6. When all nine cells are filled with no winner, the status reads `Draw`.

All six behaviors above are checked by the hidden test suite — make them all pass.

### Notes

- Don't rename files, the exported `App`, the `square` class names, the `data-testid`s (`board`, `status`, `cell-0` … `cell-8`), or the markup structure — the tests locate cells through them.
- The win-detection and turn logic in `App.jsx` / `utils/winner.js` are correct; the defect lives in how the board reports which cell was clicked. Trace the index from a click through to `handleCellClick` before touching anything else.
- The initial render must keep working — an empty, legible 3x3 grid, no crashes.
